classification.difficultyReason: Sketch the specified absolute-value graph and line, find their intersections, and select the intervals where the first graph is higher.

inlines.text: The next questions involve solving an absolute value inequality where there is a function on both sides. We must either solve it graphically or consider cases.
on the same axes, hence solve

spec.description: Unit Cartesian grid from -3 to 13 on both axes, with double-ended axes, numbered nonzero ticks and no supplied answer curves.
spec.mathematics: Both axes have unit scale. Students sketch y=|4x-5| and y=2x+3.
spec.answerVisibility: Grid and axes visible in the question edition; coloured curves belong to answers.

answer.worked:
The graphs intersect at $\left(\frac13,\frac{11}{3}\right)$ and $(4,11)$. The graph of $y=|4x-5|$ lies above $y=2x+3$ when
$$x<\frac13\quad\text{or}\quad x>4.$$

spec.description: Complete solution graph with the source coordinate scaffold, a blue absolute-value graph and a red line, each with continuation arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: y=|4x-5| has vertex (5/4,0); y=2x+3 intersects it at (1/3,11/3) and (4,11).
